company: Wärtsilä Energy Storage (RCT Solutions joint venture)
reason: The event is real and in-window (Wärtsilä stock-exchange release, 15 Jun 2026: its global Energy Storage business, about 480 employees and EUR 694 million net sales, goes into a 50/50 joint venture with RCT Solutions GmbH; Energy Storage ceases to be a reporting segment from Q2 2026; RCT's Peter Fath becomes CEO of the venture after closing), but the row's thesis, a deal-capable standalone brand scored 70 with a 6-10 week horizon, is contradicted by the same primary source. Closing was only 'expected in the third quarter of 2026' subject to regulatory approvals AND 'arrangement of a financing package'; no completion, legal name or brand has been announced as of 5 Sep 2026 (searched Wärtsilä newsroom, Inderes, Energy-Storage.News, MarketScreener), so there is no company, leadership page or marketing owner to approach. The release states the venture 'is expected to be loss-making in 2026 driven by recent low order intake as well as costs related to transformation actions, consisting mainly of write-down of capitalized R&D', with an estimated EUR -40 to -50 million impact on Wärtsilä's 2026 operating result and positive results only 'towards the end of 2027'. A carve-out arranged to stop the parent reporting a loss-making segment, still raising its financing, is not a business that funds a multi-year Formula E partnership in 2026-27; an honest score is in the 50s (capacity and urgency both weak), below the 70 threshold, so no case is built. Sponsor-table context for a future re-look: Envision Group (Envision Racing's title parent) is the grid's incumbent battery/storage name and rules that team out; Shell sits on Lola Yamaha ABT and TotalEnergies on DS Penske in the energy category; ABB is the championship title partner. No motorsport tie found for Wärtsilä or RCT leadership. Re-surface at closing, once the venture has a name, a leadership page and a financing package, and reassess against the 2027 Formula E season.
